raw_signal: לחצתי, המסך אמר REVEAL, וראיתי בדיוק אותו לוח. הייתי צריך לגלול פעם וחצי כדי למצוא מה הוא אמר לי.
observations: 390x844, after commit: the word REVEAL renders at y=236 at 14px, the position header at y=254, and then 645px of board.
The first reveal heading is at y=899, its finding sentence at y=1133, the continuation control at y=1454. Page height 1844.
Nothing in the reveal's four blocks is inside the first viewport. The page does not scroll itself.

Above the fold, the post-commit screen and the pre-commit screen carry the same masthead, the same counter strip, a 74x14px label, a header and the same board. The label text changes from DECIDE to REVEAL.
At 1440x900 the same blocks begin at y=213 and are visible without scrolling.

candidate_mechanisms.name: One column, source order, no viewport-conditional placement
candidate_mechanisms.explains: Why the desktop two-column layout puts the reveal beside the board and the handset puts it after 645px of board.
candidate_mechanisms.does_not_explain: Why no scroll-into-view or collapse accompanies the state change on the narrow layout.
candidate_mechanisms.discriminator: Measure the same reveal at 768px and 1024px. If the blocks stay below the board at every width under the two-column breakpoint, placement is purely source order.

candidate_mechanisms.name: The board is treated as the reveal's subject and therefore kept first
candidate_mechanisms.explains: Why the board stays full-size after commit and carries the move arrow and evaluation bar.
candidate_mechanisms.does_not_explain: Why the label that distinguishes the two states is 14px and the board that does not distinguish them is 405x405.
candidate_mechanisms.discriminator: Ask the owner whether the arrow and evaluation bar are intended as the handset's primary reveal, with the four text blocks secondary.

design_distinction: reveal_presented is a render event. reveal_read is a person having the finding in view. On a handset these are separated by one and a half screens of scrolling, and the funnel currently cannot tell them apart.
rejected_explanations: Slow rendering: the blocks are in the DOM within 2.2s of the press; they are placed low, not late.
A stylesheet failing on narrow viewports: the desktop and handset layouts differ deliberately and both render cleanly.
must_not_change: The four-block order and the commit-then-reveal sequence are frozen by ACQUISITION_PROTOCOL_V1. Any change to where the reveal lands changes what reveal_presented denominates, so it needs a protocol version, not a CSS fix.
perceptual_success_criterion: A person on a handset, without being told to scroll, restates one sentence from the reveal that is not the position name.
next_step: This is F-1 and it stays FIELD until a person is watched reading it. Before that: state in the protocol whether reveal_presented is defined as rendered or as in-viewport, because the two give different denominators for F-3 and the code currently supports only the first.
